issue: Is a district court's failure to advise a defendant of the knowledge-of-status element (Rehaif) at a plea colloquy a structural error that requires reversal without a showing of prejudice?

sides.position: The Rehaif knowledge-of-status error is structural and requires reversal without a showing that the defendant would have pleaded differently.
cases: United States v. Gary, 2020 WL 1443528 (4th Cir. Mar. 25, 2020)

sides.position: The Rehaif knowledge-of-status error is not structural; the defendant must show a reasonable probability he would have pleaded not guilty absent the error.
cases: United States v. Williams, 946 F.3d 968 (7th Cir. 2020)
United States v. Trujillo, 960 F.3d 1196 (10th Cir. 2020)
United States v. Tignor, 981 F.3d 826 (10th Cir. 2020)

this_court: The error is not structural, following Williams (7th Cir.) and Trujillo, and the defendant must show a reasonable probability he would have pleaded not guilty.
quote: At the time, we hadn't decided whether to characterize this error as a structural error and a circuit split existed elsewhere.
cite: United States v. Tignor, 981 F.3d 826 (10th Cir. 2020)
